metaDescription: Mio, MI mineral rights owner? Oscoda County seat on the eastern Antrim edge, honest evaluation off real production, no mailbox-offer games.
heroLead: Mio is the smallest county seat you'll deal with on this end of the state, and the mineral records for a lot of eastern Antrim-play ground run right through its courthouse.
intro: Mio, county seat of Oscoda County, sits along the Au Sable River on the eastern edge of the Antrim Shale trend, an area with real oil and gas production history but generally lighter well density than the tighter core counties like Otsego or Antrim. Land around Mio saw leasing and, in a number of sections, drilling during the boom years of the late 1980s and 1990s.

sections.heading: Eastern-edge Antrim history around Mio
paragraphs: Because Oscoda County sits toward the eastern side of the trend, activity here is a mix of genuine core-adjacent production and acreage that was only ever leased, never drilled. If your family held land near Mio through the boom years, we check whether your specific section shows recorded production before saying anything about your interest, since the two situations are worth very different amounts.
Where wells were drilled, they behave like the rest of the Antrim play, long and flat, meaning decades of small, steady volumes rather than a dramatic curve.

sections.heading: Title records and heirship around Mio
paragraphs: A lot of the private land around Mio is tied to old timber and homestead-era patents, subdivided and passed down through families for generations, with mineral rights that frequently split off from the surface somewhere in that process. The Oscoda County register of deeds in Mio holds the recorded chain of title, and it's often the first stop for an owner trying to figure out exactly what they hold.

faqs.question: Is Mio in the Antrim Shale core or on the flank?
faqs.answer: Oscoda County, where Mio is the county seat, sits on the eastern edge of the trend, a mix of genuine production and acreage that was only ever leased. We check your specific section before quoting anything.

faqs.question: How do I find out if land near Mio was ever leased or drilled?
faqs.answer: The Oscoda County register of deeds in Mio holds recorded leases and deeds, and the state's oil and gas well records can confirm whether a well was ever permitted or drilled nearby.

faqs.question: Why is my royalty check from a well near Mio so small?
faqs.answer: If the well is one of the Antrim Shale wells drilled during the 1990s boom, it's now decades into a long, flat decline, meaning small, steady volumes rather than anything close to its early production years.
